featured_reviews.review_text:
I left this appointment feeling misled and pressured, and I can't in good conscience recommend this dermatologist. I visited this dermatologist hoping for a thorough skin consultation for acne and skin health-related issues. I even paid extra for an appointment with their lead doctor, Dr. Apratim Goel.

Isotretinoin was prescribed after a rushed consultation with zero blood work or detailed diagnosis. I was told the medication was just "like a vitamin,"  which is simply not accurate. It is a potent drug with serious documented side effects, even when taken in microdoses that I only learned about through my own research after the fact. On top of that, Botox and fillers were pushed during an appointment I booked purely for acne concerns. It felt like a sales visit, not a medical one.

Patients deserve informed consent, thorough consultations, and honest explanations of what they're being prescribed. None of that happened here. I do not recommend this place to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Naomi Barton
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is an aesthetic clinic masquerading as a medical dermatologist now in a shamefully bad way that seems to be exclusively to make as much money as possible.

Very sad to see the drop in standards. Three years ago I visited for a hormonal acne complaint and had a wonderful doctor who swiftly prescribed me the necessary and low cost medication that was appropriate after conducting a proper investigation.

I took my friend here this time for a complaint and was told by the doctor that the only way to address an inflammatory autoimmune condition is homeopathy. HOMEOPATHY IS NOT MEDICINE. The doctor failed to disclose that she is not qualified under any actual medical guidelines, but only as a homeopath.

She tried to prescribe oral Tretinoin and accompanied it with a number of actives in a manner completely inappropriate to the skin condition - which was flaky and peeling rash that is either dermatitis or psoriasis. We had to insist on refusing and she did not disclose the side effects. After pushing her on other meds based on consultationsn with other doctors she then prescribed basic medication Topisal (300 bucks!!) that is actually appropriate to the condition.

She added a whole bunch of other stuff that was completely unnecessary. We have just used Topisal + Nivea Creme (Blue tin) and it has resolved everything overnight.

I am horrified that this clinic, which used to be a gold standard that I would recommend to all my friends. I would also seriously warn anyone who is using these services to first check on whether the person prescribing you medical procedures is actually qualified to do those - just because our healthcare governance and regulation has gone to the dogs doesn't mean that these charlatans are actual medical professionals, and you should protect yourselves.

Why Does Seborrheic Dermatitis Happen?
It’s not just a surface issue; it’s a combination of factors:

Yeast Overgrowth: An overgrowth of natural yeast on the skin.

Inflammatory Reaction: Triggered in highly sensitive areas.

Barrier Disruption: A compromised skin barrier, which is often worsened by winter weather, harsh shampoos, and hot showers.

Eyebrows & eyelashes

Around the nose

Beard area

Behind the ears

Upper chest

Dandruff vs. Seborrheic Dermatitis

featured_reviews.review_text:
### **Disclaimer:**

I didn’t go through with treatment because I prefer being treated by an actual doctor, not someone who seems more focused on squeezing money out of patients, especially those who may not be financially well-off. And I say that with full awareness of what “poor patients” truly means.

**My Experience:**

I’m new to the city, so I searched online for a dermatologist nearby who had good reviews. Strangely enough, this particular doctor came up as one of the top-rated in the area. The appointment process was smooth, the lady who answered the phone was polite and scheduled me for the next day, which is the day of review.

And of course, like it’s becoming all too common these days, the doctor didn’t show up on time despite the appointment.

When the doctor finally arrived, I was called in. I explained that I had a skin rash and also an issue on the scalp, both seemingly related. Without even hearing me out properly, she immediately declared, “That’s two different problems,” and proceeded to say she charges separately for each issue. I was stunned at how transactional her tone was like I’d committed a crime by showing up with two symptoms.

At that moment, I started questioning the setup. Is this how some doctors in this city operate, charging patients separately for every concern just to make more money? I even thought to myself: if I were okay paying this kind of fee, I would’ve gone to a more qualified dermatologist. Someone with a proper masters degree  and specialization not someone who’s only done a diploma course or vocational training in dermatology.

My intention was simple: to consult a regular, affordable doctor for a rash, not an overpriced cosmetologist. Ironically, this doctor was charging *more* than the high-end specialists do. I told her, “Even though I can afford it, I refuse to waste money like this,” and walked out.

### **Why I’m Sharing This:**

It’s important to understand the nature of your health problem and how much it should realistically cost to treat it. At the end of the day, it’s *your* health and *your* money. I’m glad I learned something today, and I hope this helps others stay cautious and informed too. Also please let the doctor mention her qualifications.
